history.dynasty: Maratha (patronage); part of the Shri Mangeshi Temple complex
history.period: 1560 CE shift; present complex Maratha-era (c. 1744), renovated 1890 and 1973
history.summary: The Parvati shrine is one of the subsidiary shrines within the Shri Mangeshi Temple complex at Mangeshi village, Priol. Multiple sources confirm the complex 'has shrines of Goddess Parvati and God Ganesha' alongside the main Mangesh (Shiva) shrine (Wikipedia), with rear subsidiary shrines housing Mulakeshwar, Virabhadra, Shantadurga, Lakshmi Narayan, Surya, Garuda and Kala Bhairav. Parvati is worshipped here as the consort of Mangesh, and the temple's founding legend itself centers on her (Shiva as a tiger frightening Parvati; her cry 'Trahi Mam girisha!' giving Manguesh his name). The shrine shares the complex's history: linga shifted from Kushasthali (Cortalim) in 1560, Maratha-era construction c. 1744, village donated 1739, renovations in 1890 and 1973. The media image shows the Mangeshi complex, not the Parvati shrine specifically (no dedicated image of the shrine was found).

name: Parvati shrine, Mangeshi temple complex
town_description: Mangeshi is a village in Priol, Ponda taluka, North Goa (PIN 403404), about 21 km from Panaji on the Panaji–Ponda road (NH 4A). It takes its name from the Shri Mangeshi Temple, one of Goa's largest and most visited Hindu shrines, and functions largely as a temple town with pilgrim lodging (agrashalas), shops and restaurants around the temple complex. The CSV town 'Mangeshi (Priol)' combines the village with Priol, the nearby larger settlement; the temple stands at Mangeshi village itself.

travel.railway: Karmali railway station, about 20 km, or Madgaon, about 26–30 km (verify)
travel.road: About 21 km from Panaji and 12 km north of Ponda on the Panaji–Ponda highway; well connected by bus and cab

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; also during the January Jatra, Maha Shivaratri and Shigmo
